ee573d7a52033235409fa14273b9f3b6d267a3a9: Bellwald is a low-key resort on a modest scale: 20 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where you come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Bellwald's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a good-natured atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. With a summit at 2558 m and a village at 1600 m, snow reliability at Bellwald is generally dependable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can create tension early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly once serious snowfalls arrive. A stay in Bellwald is clearly expensive: 58€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but be aware of it before you go. In short, Bellwald does not rival the giants of skiing and does not pretend to. It is an honest, often underrated destination that deserves to be (re)discovered.

eef17abfc08dd20f5d21631cdfa806091607058b: Flaine offers 146 km of well-marked runs, a medium-sized ski area ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 34 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in high season. Flaine's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Flaine's altitude (1600 m at the bottom, 2480 m at the top) helps it maintain decent snow cover in the depths of winter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it's best to check conditions before finalising a booking. A stay in Flaine is clearly expensive: 61€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the priciest in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Flaine keeps its promises. It's a Northern Alps resort that will suit most profiles without disappointing.
